<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
After looking into the problem it became clear that the issue was not caused by pandas but by the data given to it. For the specific issue linked to this PR (#4927), in the set of indicator data points being converted to a `DataFrame` there was a property called `PercentB` for the BollingerBand indicator, this property had repeated index values after the date 4/18 which caused the Value Error. 

This property uses `CompositeIndicator` which was found to not fill forward properly and update the properties time. With these changes, if the conditions to update the `CompositeIndicator` are not met, it now creates a clone of the last point with the latest time. This way the indicator current.Time is always up to date.

@C-SELLERS I have merged your changes to [my own fork](https://github.com/athon-millane/Lean) and am still seeing the same error as #4927 in my notebook. I gather this would be because the base image isn't updated, if I want to spin my own image is this as simple as building from [this Dockerfile](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/DockerfileJupyter) with the updated code?

Thanks

Hey Athon! Yeah you will have to build the new image for it to work, you'll have to do two actually because the research image builds off of the Lean image. 

So first build the Linux version of Lean; you can use `"/p:ForceLinuxBuild=true"` if on windows; then build the Lean Docker image with this [DockerFile](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Dockerfile), then finally build the research image with this [DockerFile](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/DockerfileJupyter#L7) but be sure to the FROM statement to the new Lean image you created in the previous step. 

Then you should be good to go! If using the launch scripts make sure you enter your custom image name!

issue_context.title: Research :  ValueError: cannot reindex from a duplicate axis
issue_context.body:
When running the provided BasicQuantBookTemplate.ipynb example in the research docker, the example stops at

```
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ValueError                                Traceback (most recent call last)
<ipython-input-3-2be348dae713> in <module>
      4 
      5 # Gets historical data of indicator
----> 6 bbdf = qb.Indicator(bb, "SPY", 360, Resolution.Daily)
      7 
      8 # drop undesired fields

ValueError: cannot reindex from a duplicate axis
```

#### Expected Behavior

The example notebook functions

#### Actual Behavior

The example notebook has a non-recoverable error

#### Reproducing the Problem

1. Follow instructions for Research docker installation
2. Start above example

#### System Information

MacOS X 10.15.7
Research docker image : ba23f2aa50f9

#### Checklist

- [X] I have completely filled out this template
- [X] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [X] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
- [X] I have provided detailed steps to reproduce the issue
comments:
Is there a difference between the environment used in the research container and the one used on the web?

Just came across this issue and noticed that the line `bbdf = qb.Indicator(bb, "SPY", 360, Resolution.Daily)` works as expected if run on the web.
No, but because the web IDE has access to QC data storage the issue does not reproduce.

Take a look at #4944 which attempted to address this issue.

The bug comes from a sub indicator of the BB being filled forwarded when it runs out of data. When its filled forwarded the date is the same for those points, and when pandas attempts to place this in a matrix it throws the error about duplicate entries for one index (date)

Locally only the data included in the repo or separately downloaded is available to use which is why it fills forward when it gets past the included data. In the cloud it has access to QC's data storage which is updated daily so it does not occur.

I think that if the column names are not already sorted, this will give back the dataframe with the wrong column names.

Let's make a test to make sure that the column names are in the order we expect 👍

That's exactly what I was thinking in the conversation with Martin above, but upon testing it, it actually matched the columns to the correct values in the dictionary. I'll go ahead and figure a way to add a test to confirm that behavior.

Cool! We need a nice collection of tests around this. 
I think during _each_ update, we will always come through this `if` because Right/Left not updated sequentially but first one and later the other? Maybe we need some extra logic for that case?

I just added two tests to show how the time on the consolidator advances. One of them `TimeAdvancedWithDataToOnlyOneSide`  is red/green'd from master to this branch. I am also adding one now for checking the data point after one update (since it shouldn't change until both are received) and after.

The pre existing `if` statement that I added the `else` to takes care of them not being updated sequentially by tracking new datapoints for either side, once both have a new datapoint it will updated.

Would like to know a bit more detailed _why_ is this required:
- Why is there `repeated index values after the date 4/18`
- Why should the composite indicator FF values, he is already triggering an event when a new value is available, so it sounds more like an issue in the consumer side 🤔
